title: Survey warmth gave no clear repeated link to nearby ozone-site differences in four US bird-route samples in 2005-2019
abstract: We tested whether survey-start temperature was linked to the absolute difference between nearby ozone sites. We used 1,599 selected bird-route windows in California, Oregon, New York and Pennsylvania in 2005-2019. Four models controlled site pair, year, survey date and start time. Mean ozone differences were 2.61-4.50 ppb. Slopes ranged from -0.13 to +0.25 ppb per 5 C. All four adjusted intervals included zero. Complete-date and largest-network checks gave no clear repeated link. This does not establish equal exposure error across temperatures. Survey-start temperature is not prior-month weather. Selected routes, few large site networks and possible shared weather limit inference. This is an exposure-method test. It does not estimate bird harm or climate-change effects. The package gives daily evidence, source hashes, code and independent numerical checks.

display.caption: Absolute ozone-site difference slopes for four selected route-survey samples. Pair and year controls; network-cluster intervals adjusted for four tests. These slopes do not measure a climate effect or bird harm.

citations.reason: Verified source of daily ozone evidence, survey windows, raw source hashes and build code. The raw observations overlap.
Prior episode-agreement test; the present study tests survey-temperature slopes of absolute monthly mean differences.
